evals.name: idea-with-no-evidence
evals.prompt: i'm a dental hygienist and ive been thinking about building an app that helps practices handle patient recalls — right now everyone i work with just uses a spreadsheet and phone calls and its a mess. i want to build it but idk if its actually a real business or just me being annoyed at my job. where do i start
evals.expected_output: Should pressure-test at the pre-product stage (Q1/Q2/Q3 only), find no external evidence, and route to customer conversations rather than producing a score or verdict. Should not invent a scorecard from nothing.

evals.name: real-numbers-in-hand
evals.prompt: ok so i put up a landing page for my contractor invoicing tool two weeks ago and drove traffic from a few facebook groups. 340 people hit the page and 41 gave me their email. nobody has paid anything yet. i know the problem is real because ive been a contractor for 9 years. should i build it or keep testing
evals.expected_output: Should compute the 12% signup rate, score the six dimensions from evidence, score willingness to pay at 1 because a waitlist signup costs the person nothing, and declare the verdict the band its own total falls in — not a verdict chosen in advance. Should name a pre-sale as the single next test and archive the brief. The check that matters is internal consistency: the verdict must match the printed score.

evals.name: enthusiasm-mistaken-for-demand
evals.prompt: i showed my idea to like 15 people at a conference last month and literally everyone said theyd use it. its a scheduling tool for physical therapy clinics. i've got a prototype half built in lovable. am i good to go all in on this
evals.expected_output: Should recognise 'everyone said they'd use it' as interest rather than demand, decline to treat it as Q1 evidence, and name a concrete willingness-to-pay test before any go-ahead.

evals.name: near-miss-should-route-elsewhere
evals.prompt: ive got paying customers now (like 30ish) and theyre all asking for different stuff — bulk export, a mobile app, and some kind of team permissions thing. i cant build all three. how do i figure out which one is actually worth doing first
evals.expected_output: Should recognise this is feature prioritisation for a product with paying customers, not demand validation, and route to the prioritize skill instead of running a validation brief.
